n01_cold
Almost everything we three-D print has to fit something real. A shelf. A drawer. A board that needs a home. Today, that means a caliper, a desktop CAD program, and a few failed prints.
n02_title
AstraCAD Spatial puts a verified CAD bench on your desk, in mixed reality.
n03_arrive
The bench appears in front of you and anchors itself to your room. A guide lights up the next thing to do.
n04_shape
Pinch a handle and pull. Every change is rebuilt, and checked against an exact formula, so the volume you see is the volume you print.
n05_voice
Or just say what you need. Speech is recognised on the device, and a small on-device language model works out which part you mean. The sizes come only from your words.
n06_box
That box has filleted corners and shelled walls.
n07_parts
There are sweeps and lofts too, each proven against Pappus' theorem and the prismatoid formula. Not just drawn. Verified.
n08_test
Then test it. Point, pinch, and a stress solver, checked against the Calculix reference solver, colours the part. Three engineering agents read the result, and offer fixes you can take with a pinch.
n09_flow
Watch the air move around it. It is an ideal flow preview, and the app tells you exactly what it cannot show.
n10_drawing
Then take it with you. A dimensioned drawing, an S T L, a three M F, or a link that opens on your phone.
n11_lineup
It runs in the Quest browser, with no account and no server. It works offline, holds its frame rate under load, and fits its layout to the narrow view of Meta's glasses.
n12_finale
AstraCAD Spatial. Measure the real thing. Get the part that fits.
